hero.headline: Draft picks power new-look St. Lucie Mets in 14-6 rout of Dunedin
hero.teaser: Four 2026 draft picks combined for nine hits and three home runs, while Clay Holmes threw four scoreless innings in a rehab appearance.
hero.body:
Four members of the New York Mets’ 2026 draft class made immediate impacts Tuesday night as the St. Lucie Mets overwhelmed the Dunedin Blue Jays 14-6 at TD Ballpark.

Aiden Robbins, Ryan Tayman, John Smith III and Kooper Schulte combined to go 9-for-17 with three home runs, two doubles, seven RBIs and seven runs scored in their professional debuts. The St. Lucie lineup also featured Yovanny Rodriguez and Wyatt Vincent, who made their team debuts after being promoted from the Florida Complex League.

The revamped offense provided more than enough support for New York Mets pitcher Clay Holmes, who moved his rehabilitation assignment from Triple-A Syracuse to the Florida State League because of predicted bad weather in New York.

Holmes, recovering from a right fibula injury, scattered two singles and two walks over four scoreless innings. He struck out three and threw 59 pitches.

Tayman gave St. Lucie a 2-0 lead in the second inning by hitting a two-run home run on the first swing of his professional career. The ninth-round selection out of Cal Poly finished 4-for-5 with a homer, a double, two singles, three runs scored and two RBIs.

Robbins, a third-round pick from Texas, drove an RBI double off the center-field wall in the third inning for his first professional hit.

The Mets added three runs in the fourth. Cole Mathis delivered a sacrifice fly before Marco Vargas lined a two-run double off the left-field wall against Dunedin starter Blake Purnell, extending the lead to 6-0.

Smith, a 19th-round pick from UCF, hit a two-run homer off Purnell in the fifth inning for his first professional hit. He homered again in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs.

Austin Warren, beginning a rehabilitation assignment for a right forearm strain, pitched a scoreless fifth inning with one strikeout and induced a double play. He was credited with the win.

Dunedin scored four runs against Tyler McLoughlin in the sixth, but Ernesto Mercedes stopped the rally with consecutive strikeouts. Mercedes then retired the Blue Jays in order in the seventh and added two more strikeouts.

Elian Peña hit a two-run homer in the eighth, and Robbins added an RBI single to push St. Lucie’s lead to 11-4.

The Mets scored three more runs in the ninth on Smith’s second homer, a bases-loaded walk by Julio Zayas and an RBI single from Vargas. Vargas finished 3-for-5 with three RBIs.

Schulte, a 20th-round pick from Iowa, went 1-for-3 with a single, a walk, a hit-by-pitch and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs in his St. Lucie debut, while Vincent went 1-for-4 with a double, a walk and a run.

The Mets improved to 12-18 in the second half and 45-51 overall. Dunedin fell to 14-16 in the second half and 44-51 overall.

The teams continue the series Wednesday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Chief warns property tax reform could force closure of fire stations, cut 116 firefighters
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli warned commissioners Tuesday that proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force sweeping cuts to fire and rescue operations in Martin County. The reform would expand homestead exemptions, potentially reducing the department's budget and forcing major reductions in service.

Among the potential cuts outlined by the chief are closing firehouses, ending hazmat, dive, and technical rescue programs, grounding the department's critical care helicopter, and using firefighting tools past their operational lifetime. The department could be forced to cut as many as 116 firefighters over the next two years, about one-third of its workforce. County documents show about 93% of the Fire Rescue budget is dedicated to personnel.

Residents who attended the commission meeting had mixed reactions. One resident said fire service is a valuable thing that matters more than other services. Another resident questioned why cutting personnel pay to make up the shortfall was not part of the options. Commissioner Edward Ciampi said the county would need to do belt tightening and slashing of budgets elsewhere. Commissioner Eileen Vargas said the county only has so many dollars to go around and needs to tighten up.

No decisions were made Tuesday. The presentation was an opportunity to gather information so the county can plan accordingly ahead of the November vote. Commissioner James Blake Capps said shutting down three fire stations could lead to higher insurance premiums for residents living more than five miles from a fire station and could increase response times with serious consequences for residents. Voters will have the final say on the constitutional amendment during the November general election.

cards.headline: Florida carries out first double execution in more than six decades, including second-oldest prisoner in U.S. history
cards.body:
Florida executed two men on Tuesday, becoming the first state in nearly a decade to carry out two executions in a single day. The second execution was of 80-year-old Dominick Anthony Occhicone, the second-oldest inmate known to receive a lethal injection in modern U.S. history. Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis, who has the authority under Florida law to set execution dates, scheduled both executions hours apart earlier this month.

Occhicone was pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m. at Florida State Prison near Starke following a three-drug injection. His execution came nearly five hours after James Aren Duckett, 68, a former police officer convicted of raping and drowning 11-year-old Teresa McAbee in central Florida in 1987, received a lethal dose in the same death chamber. Duckett was pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m. and declined to make a final statement. Occhicone, convicted of fatally shooting his ex-girlfriend's parents in June 1986, apologized to the victims' families and his own family in his final words. He is the oldest prisoner executed in Florida since the state began modern record-keeping a century ago. Nationwide, only 83-year-old Walter Moody Jr., executed in Alabama in 2018, was older.

The executions mark the 11th and 12th carried out by Florida this year. The state has conducted more executions in 2026 than all other states combined. DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the U.S. reinstatement of the death penalty in 1976. Another execution is scheduled for August. Nationwide, 19 executions have been carried out this year, with Florida accounting for 12. The last time a state carried out two executions in one day was in 2017, when Arkansas put two men to death three hours apart.

Florida Department of Corrections records show multiple executions on a single day were more common in the past, with the last occurring in 1964. The U.S. Supreme Court denied last appeals from both men Tuesday. DeSantis has rarely commented on the pace of executions, previously noting some on death row had committed crimes as far back as the 1980s. He said last year that justice delayed is justice denied. All Florida executions are by injection of a sedative, a paralytic and a drug that stops the heart.

cards.headline: Martin County commissioners to hear Fire Rescue impact presentation on proposed homestead exemption expansion
cards.teaser: Martin County commissioners are expected to hear a presentation outlining how a proposed expansion of Florida's homestead exemption could affect Martin County Fire Rescue if voters approve the constitutional amendment on the November ballot.
cards.body:
The presentation is expected to focus on the projected financial impact of the proposed tax changes and what they could mean for the department's budget, staffing, operations and emergency response. Commissioner James Blake Capps said he will honor the will of the voters, whatever they decide regarding the proposed constitutional amendment, but expressed concerns about the depth of the cuts needed as they relate to government operations, particularly fire rescue.

Fire Rescue leaders are expected to discuss potential operational changes if revenue reductions occur. Previous county projections have outlined possible station closures, reductions to specialized teams including HAZMAT, Technical Rescue, the dive team and LifeStar, and delays in replacing equipment. Officials have warned the proposed cuts could lead to longer emergency response times and affect specialized emergency services provided throughout Martin County.

Capps said another serious consequence for Martin County residents would be higher insurance premiums. If a resident is within five miles of a fire station, they receive a break on homeowner's insurance, but if farther than five miles away, they pay higher premiums. He said if the county shuts down three fire stations, a lot of people would end up paying more for homeowner's insurance. The meeting starts at 9 a.m.

He declined to make a final statement and showed no response several minutes into the execution when the prison warden shook him and shouted his name. Duckett became the 11th Florida inmate executed this year.

The girl's relatives spoke of decades of suffering after the execution. Dorthy Tula, the victim's mother, said she waited nearly 40 years to have him dead before breaking down. Tracy Mcfall-Buskirk, the girl's cousin, said the man took advantage of his badge. The execution was part of the first double execution in Florida in more than six decades and the first time any state has carried out two executions in one day since Arkansas in 2017.

Florida has now conducted 12 executions to date in 2026, more than all other states combined. Gov. Ron DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the reinstatement of the death penalty in the U.S. in 1976.

cards.headline: New $70 million K-8 school breaks ground in Fort Pierce, will consolidate three St. Lucie County campuses
cards.body:
A groundbreaking ceremony Tuesday marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one state-of-the-art facility. The new school will be built on land behind Dan McCarty Middle School and is expected to welcome between 1,500 and 1,800 students when it opens. It will consolidate Dan McCarty Middle, St. Lucie Elementary and Lawnwood Elementary into a single campus.

Superintendent Jon Prince said the project is moving forward on time, on budget, and on schedule. The new facility will feature state-of-the-art technology and serve the north part of St. Lucie County. The decision to consolidate comes as the existing schools show their age. All three were built in the 1950s and 1960s. Dan McCarty Middle Principal Latricia Stubbs-James said some of the things in the buildings are antiquated and that students in the northern part of the county are getting the attention they deserve and need.

The district is funding the $70 million project in part by selling the properties where the three older schools currently stand, offsetting the cost of maintaining aging buildings. Prince said the K-8 model is already proven across the district, which operates 11 other K-8 schools. Attendance is better, test scores are better and grades are better in the K-8s, Prince said. Stubbs-James said the K-8 model offers unique benefits, allowing kindergarten students to see what it looks like to be an eighth grader or a fifth grader.

The new Fort Pierce K-8 school is expected to be completed in August 2028. Prince said the facility will be very popular in the community.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie men flee police at 80 mph, one found hiding on roof of occupied home
cards.teaser: Two men led Port St. Lucie police on a high-speed chase before abandoning their car and fleeing on foot Monday, with one suspect found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
A suspected drunk driver fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran. According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving on Southwest Becker Road. Instead of pulling over, the driver accelerated and weaved in and out of traffic, ignoring traffic signs and signals.

 The driver and passenger abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot. A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.

 The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46. Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie opens $28.8 million police training facility
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie cut the ribbon on a 54,283-square-foot police training center featuring a 20-lane indoor firearms range, tactical shoot house and virtual simulation theater.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie officially opened a 54,283-square-foot, $28.8 million police training center on July 24 on the grounds of City Hall, just northwest of the police department. Mayor Shannon Martin said the project is about making sure officers have the space, training and resources needed to serve the community at the highest level. The facility took four years to construct.

 The three-story facility includes a 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range featuring an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system, a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms for realistic scenario-based training, and a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for immersive decision-making and de-escalation exercises. The facility also includes a dedicated defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology, a multi-purpose training room for classroom instruction and conferences, and three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division with 19 offices and 86 workstations. Officer Brittany McNally said the facility will reduce recurring costs from sending officers to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training while allowing the department to train more efficiently and effectively.

cards.headline: Martin County projects $16.5 million annual Fire Rescue budget loss under proposed homestead exemption
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Rescue projects its annual budget would decline by $9.5 million in the first year if voters approve expanded homestead exemptions in November.
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue projects its annual budget would decline by $9.5 million in the first year under a proposed expansion of Florida's homestead exemption. By the second year, the annual loss would reach $16.5 million, a 22% reduction from the department's current budget. Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli presented the planning exercise during Tuesday's commission meeting.

 Under the scenario, Fire Rescue could close Station 18 on Britt Road, Station 33 in Hobe Sound, and Station 23 on Kanner Highway. The department could be forced to lay off as many as 116 firefighters by the second year, equivalent to one of the department's three shifts. The funding loss could force Martin County to eliminate specialized teams responsible for hazardous materials incidents, technical rescues and dive operations.

 Cianciulli pointed to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in Texas as an example of delays that can occur when a community must rely on outside resources. In an interview after the meeting, Cianciulli said they had to call for outside assets, a 14 hour response to start mitigating that scene. He said Martin County is in a position where if any incident happens, they are able to do an immediate mitigation without wasting any second.

hero.headline: Three arrested in Fort Pierce after 3-month-old dies from dehydration, malnutrition
hero.body:
Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce in August 2025. Nicole Maxwell, the child's mother, Robert Maxwell, the child's grandfather, and Vikki Koon, the grandfather's girlfriend, were arrested last week following a nearly year-long investigation by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

The investigation began on Aug. 20, 2025, when deputies responded to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital after Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the infant to the emergency room. The child was pronounced dead on arrival. A medical examiner later determined the baby died from dehydration and malnutrition and ruled the death a homicide. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach, and the child exhibited lesions consistent with severe dehydration.

The infant lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon at a mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle in Fort Pierce, while Nicole Maxwell lived with a boyfriend in Vero Beach. St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Detective Jennifer Diaz described the mobile home as having windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring, and live and dead cockroaches throughout. The home was extremely hot, with a bug infestation, lack of food, and unsafe conditions for walking, Diaz said. Koon told investigators she fed the infant only twice a day and when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with baby cereal mixed in.

Four other children of Nicole Maxwell who were living in the home, ranging in age from 2 to 10 years old, have been placed in foster care through the state Department of Children and Families. Robert Maxwell and Koon are held at the St. Lucie County Jail, each on $1.5 million bond. Nicole Maxwell was arrested July 23 at a home in the 300 block of 12th Street, SW, Vero Beach, and is held at the Indian River County Jail on no bond. A neighbor named Suzan said she witnessed the children asking for water and food, describing the conditions as unlivable.

cards.headline: Man forced to withdraw cash during armed robbery at Fort Pierce Wells Fargo ATM
cards.teaser: Two men forced a customer to withdraw cash at gunpoint from a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce Sunday night before fleeing on foot.
cards.body:
A man using a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce became the victim of an armed robbery Sunday at about 8:38 p.m. when two men approached him and forced him to withdraw cash. One suspect displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department.

Officers responded to the scene, established a perimeter, and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects. The suspects were not located. Police described them as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie bans gas station on Tradition commercial site after months of resident concerns
hero.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council has permanently banned construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive in Tradition. The council unanimously approved the restriction on July 13 as part of the 16th amendment to the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development, ending nearly three months of debate over the future of land originally planned as Phase 3 of the Heritage Oaks at Tradition residential development.

Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission in May to convert the parcel from residential to commercial use. While council members supported commercial development, several raised concerns that a convenience store with gas pumps would worsen traffic along Crosstown Parkway west of Interstate 95. Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo and other council members asked staff to determine whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use, leading the council to table the request on May 26. Heritage Oaks residents urged the council in June to reject the land-use change, citing traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts.

The council voted 4-0 on June 22 to approve the commercial designation after the developer agreed to permanently give up the right to build a gas station. The July 13 ordinance codified that restriction into the Tradition MPUD documents, ensuring the prohibition remains with the property regardless of future ownership. City planner Bridget Kean said service stations remain permitted elsewhere in the Tradition mixed-use area but are now prohibited on Parcel 11A. The updated plan also requires the developer to install a fence along the southern property line before mass grading and to complete an architectural wall and landscape buffering along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued.

Councilman Anthony Bonna defended the public process and the decision, saying Port St. Lucie has long lacked commercial development, placing a burden on homeowners. Councilman David Pickett said the city has consistently heard residents oppose additional housing and called the shift to commercial the best outcome for the corner. Councilwoman Stephanie Morgan, who initially questioned whether prohibiting a specific business type amounted to government interference, ultimately voted with the council. Mayor Shannon Martin confirmed the restriction would remain with the property in perpetuity before the final unanimous vote.

cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli told commissioners Tuesday that proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force sweeping cuts including closing firehouses, ending specialized rescue programs and cutting up to 116 firefighters.
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli warned commissioners Tuesday that proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force sweeping cuts to fire and rescue operations. The reform would expand homestead exemptions, potentially reducing the department's budget and forcing major reductions in service.

Cianciulli outlined potential cuts including closing firehouses, ending hazmat, dive and technical rescue programs, grounding the department's critical care helicopter, and using firefighting tools past their operational lifetime. The department could be forced to cut as many as 116 firefighters over the next two years. Cianciulli said losing firefighters would be a detriment to the organization and the community.

Commissioners expressed differing views on how to respond if the reform passes. Commissioner Edward Ciampi said the county would be doing belt tightening and slashing of budgets elsewhere. Commissioner Eileen Vargas said the county only has so many dollars to go around. No decisions were made Tuesday. The presentation was an opportunity to gather information so the county can plan ahead of the November vote.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie bans gas station on 9.4-acre Tradition commercial parcel after resident concerns
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council unanimously approved an ordinance on July 13 that permanently prohibits construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwe
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council unanimously approved an ordinance on July 13 that permanently prohibits construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive in the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development. The council vote was the second and final reading of the 16th amendment to the Tradition MPUD, codifying a restriction that bars any current or future owner from developing a service station on the site.

 The amendment changes the parcel's designation from residential to commercial, clearing the way for retail and office development while addressing concerns raised by Heritage Oaks at Tradition residents about traffic and congestion. Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission to convert what had been planned as Phase 3 of the Heritage Oaks residential development into commercial property. During the initial May 26 quasi-judicial hearing, Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo and other council members noted increasing congestion along the commercial corridor and asked staff to determine whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use.

 Several Heritage Oaks residents urged the council at the June 22 hearing to reject the land-use change, citing concerns about increased traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts. The council voted 4-0 to approve the commercial designation on first reading after the developer agreed to permanently relinquish the right to build a gas station. City planner Bridget Kean said the updated development plan specifies that while service stations remain a permitted use elsewhere within the mixed-use area, they are prohibited on Parcel 11A.

 Before any mass grading begins, the developer must install a fence along the southern property line to prevent construction access through Southwest Glenbrook Drive, which connects to Heritage Oaks. An architectural wall and landscape buffering must be completed along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued for vertical construction.

 Councilman Anthony Bonna defended the public process and said expanding commercial development will benefit residents by broadening the city's tax base. Councilman David Pickett said he was excited about the residential-to-commercial conversion. Mayor Shannon Martin asked staff to confirm that the prohibition would remain with the property regardless of ownership. Kean confirmed the restriction is now written directly into the Tradition MPUD documents, ensuring no future owner can develop a gas station on the parcel.

cards.headline: $70 million K-8 school breaks ground in Fort Pierce, combining three aging St. Lucie County campuses
cards.teaser: A groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one state-of-the-art facility. T
cards.body:
A groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one state-of-the-art facility. The new school will be built on land behind Dan McCarty Middle School and is expected to welcome between 1,500 and 1,800 students when it opens. It will consolidate Dan McCarty Middle, St. Lucie Elementary and Lawnwood Elementary into a single campus.

 Superintendent Jon Prince said the project is moving forward on time, on budget and on schedule. Prince said the new facility will feature state-of-the-art technology and serve the north part of St. Lucie County. The decision to consolidate comes as the existing schools show their age.

 All three were built in the 1950s and 1960s. Dan McCarty Middle Principal Latricia Stubbs-James said the wear and tear is visible inside the building and some of the things in there are antiquated.

 The district is funding the $70 million project in part by selling the properties where the three older schools currently stand, offsetting the cost of maintaining aging buildings. Prince said the K-8 model is already proven across the district, which operates 11 other K-8 schools. Attendance is better, test scores are better and grades are better in the K-8s, Prince said.

 Stubbs-James said the K-8 model offers unique benefits for younger students. Kindergarten students can see what it looks like to be an eighth grader at a new K-8, and what it looks like to be a fifth grader, Stubbs-James said. The new Fort Pierce K-8 school is expected to be completed in August 2028.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents oppose proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe over concerns for St. Lucie County Regional History Museum
cards.teaser: Residents and history advocates in Fort Pierce are raising concerns over a proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe, fearing the development could displace the area's cultural heritage and the St. Lucie County Regional History Museum.
cards.body:
The Port of Fort Pierce master plan draft for 2026 calls for replacing the existing area at Museum Pointe with large floating docks designed for mega yachts, along with a clubhouse, an event center and a water taxi connecting to Harbour Pointe to the north. The plan also proposes relocating the history museum. Terry Howard, a passionate advocate for St. Lucie County's history, expressed disbelief over the proposed changes.

 This is a gem for the area, and I just can't believe they want to put mega yachts here, he said. The museum, it's our culture. It's the center for our culture for this county.

 In a statement, St. Lucie County said that no plans have been approved and feedback from the board will dictate future changes, modifications and clarifications to the draft document. Howard has started a petition opposing the proposed marina, hoping to raise awareness and preserve the location and its natural surroundings. This is just a really fantastic place, and our history is capsulized in this museum here, he said. The draft of the master plan is expected to go before the county commission in August.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County school district cuts 19 workers as Temporary Protected Status expires
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County School District is separating 19 employees from employment today as Temporary Protected Status expires for Haitian workers.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County confirmed 19 district employees will be separated from employment as all school district employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Chuck Ridley, director of civic engagement for the Service Employees International Union, said the union expects hundreds of workers statewide to be affected, with nearly 20 employees in the Palm Beach County School District alone.

 Ridley said many of the workers losing TPS protections are bus drivers, custodians, paraprofessionals, food service employees and city workers. He warned that without drivers to pick up students or workers to provide public services, residents will see disruptions in schools, garbage collection and other city functions. The healthcare system could also face staffing shortages, particularly in hospitals and nursing homes that rely heavily on immigrant workers.

 The Florida Healthcare Association said Haitian caregivers are valued members of the long term care workforce, serving as certified nursing assistants, nurses, dietary aides, housekeepers and other essential team members. The association said a disruption to experienced staff could create additional challenges to long term care centers focused on supporting the needs of residents, families and care teams. According to the Lar Management Group, the Haitian community contributes an estimated $1.2 billion to Florida's economy.

hero.headline: Draft picks power new-look St. Lucie Mets in 14-6 rout of Dunedin
hero.teaser: Four 2026 draft picks combined for nine hits and three home runs, while Clay Holmes threw four scoreless innings in a rehab appearance.
hero.body:
Four members of the New York Mets’ 2026 draft class made immediate impacts Tuesday night as the St. Lucie Mets overwhelmed the Dunedin Blue Jays 14-6 at TD Ballpark.

Aiden Robbins, Ryan Tayman, John Smith III and Kooper Schulte combined to go 9-for-17 with three home runs, two doubles, seven RBIs and seven runs scored in their professional debuts. The St. Lucie lineup also featured Yovanny Rodriguez and Wyatt Vincent, who made their team debuts after being promoted from the Florida Complex League.

The revamped offense provided more than enough support for New York Mets pitcher Clay Holmes, who moved his rehabilitation assignment from Triple-A Syracuse to the Florida State League because of predicted bad weather in New York.

Holmes, recovering from a right fibula injury, scattered two singles and two walks over four scoreless innings. He struck out three and threw 59 pitches.

Tayman gave St. Lucie a 2-0 lead in the second inning by hitting a two-run home run on the first swing of his professional career. The ninth-round selection out of Cal Poly finished 4-for-5 with a homer, a double, two singles, three runs scored and two RBIs.

Robbins, a third-round pick from Texas, drove an RBI double off the center-field wall in the third inning for his first professional hit.

The Mets added three runs in the fourth. Cole Mathis delivered a sacrifice fly before Marco Vargas lined a two-run double off the left-field wall against Dunedin starter Blake Purnell, extending the lead to 6-0.

Smith, a 19th-round pick from UCF, hit a two-run homer off Purnell in the fifth inning for his first professional hit. He homered again in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs.

Austin Warren, beginning a rehabilitation assignment for a right forearm strain, pitched a scoreless fifth inning with one strikeout and induced a double play. He was credited with the win.

Dunedin scored four runs against Tyler McLoughlin in the sixth, but Ernesto Mercedes stopped the rally with consecutive strikeouts. Mercedes then retired the Blue Jays in order in the seventh and added two more strikeouts.

Elian Peña hit a two-run homer in the eighth, and Robbins added an RBI single to push St. Lucie’s lead to 11-4.

The Mets scored three more runs in the ninth on Smith’s second homer, a bases-loaded walk by Julio Zayas and an RBI single from Vargas. Vargas finished 3-for-5 with three RBIs.

Schulte, a 20th-round pick from Iowa, went 1-for-3 with a single, a walk, a hit-by-pitch and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs in his St. Lucie debut, while Vincent went 1-for-4 with a double, a walk and a run.

The Mets improved to 12-18 in the second half and 45-51 overall. Dunedin fell to 14-16 in the second half and 44-51 overall.

The teams continue the series Wednesday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named Florida State League Pitcher of the Week
cards.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for the week of July 20-26. Minor League Baseball announced the honor on Tuesday.

Ware made two appearances last week at Clover Park against Fort Myers, one start on Tuesday and one relief outing on Sunday. The southpaw combined to pitch 7.0 scoreless innings. He scattered three hits, walked two and struck out 12. The Mets won both games with Ware getting credit for the win on Sunday.

Ware, 22, was drafted by the Mets in the 15th round out of LSU in 2025. He made his pro debut with St. Lucie in April and has been with the team all season.

This is the first FSL Pitcher or Player of the Week award for the Mets this season.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named FSL Pitcher of the Week
cards.teaser: The 22-year-old left-hander struck out 12 batters over seven scoreless innings in two appearances against Fort Myers.
cards.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced Monday.

 Ware made two appearances against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels at Clover Park, starting Tuesday and returning for a relief outing Sunday. The left-hander combined to throw seven scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two walks while striking out 12 batters.

 The Mets won both games in which Ware appeared. He earned the victory Sunday after pitching four scoreless innings, allowing one hit and one walk and recording a career-high eight strikeouts as St. Lucie rallied for an 11-8 win.

 Ware, 22, was selected by the New York Mets in the 15th round of the 2025 MLB Draft out of LSU. He made his professional debut with St. Lucie in April and has remained with the team throughout the season.

cards.headline: Mets erase 5-0 deficit to beat Mighty Mussels 11-8
cards.teaser: Jeremy Rodriguez went 4-for-4, and Conner Ware struck out a career-high eight as St. Lucie scored eight runs in the second inning.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets erased an early five-run deficit with an eight-run second inning and rallied for an 11-8 win over the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Sunday afternoon at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers won the seven-game series 4-3 and finished the season series with an 8-4 advantage.

 The Mighty Mussels scored three runs in the first inning and two more in the second to build a 5-0 lead. St. Lucie responded with eight runs in the bottom of the second and moved ahead for good.

 Randy Guzman delivered the decisive hit, lining a two-out, two-run single that turned a 5-4 deficit into a 6-5 Mets lead. Julio Zayas followed with a two-run single to extend the advantage to 8-5.

 The Mets added three runs in the third. Elian Peña hit an RBI single, Jacob Reimer drove in a run with a double and Trey Snyder added a sacrifice fly to make it 11-5.

 Conner Ware took over on the mound in the third inning and settled the game down for St. Lucie. Ware pitched four scoreless innings, allowed one hit and one walk, and struck out a career-high eight batters. He struck out the side swinging in the fourth and struck out the side looking in the sixth before earning the win.

 Fort Myers scored three runs in the seventh against Luis Sotillo, who was making his Mets debut. Sotillo recovered by retiring six of the final seven batters he faced and carried the game through the eighth inning.

 Elwis Mijares worked a perfect ninth on six pitches to record his third save.

 Jeremy Rodriguez led the Mets at the plate, going 4-for-4 with a double, an RBI and two runs scored from the No. 9 spot in the order. Zayas and Peña collected two hits apiece.

 Reimer, beginning a minor league rehabilitation assignment for a groin injury, went 1-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and two runs scored. He played all nine innings at third base.

 The Mets improved to 11-18 in the second half and 44-51 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game road series against the Dunedin Blue Jays on Tuesday. First pitch at TD Ballpark is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Fall Short in 15-14 Loss to Fort Myers
cards.teaser: Randy Guzman hit two home runs and drove in six as the St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run deficit in a 15-14 loss to Fort Myers.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run first-inning deficit but fell one run short in a 15-14 loss to the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Saturday night at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers scored eight runs in the opening inning and survived several St. Lucie rallies to earn its third consecutive victory.

 Mets starter Ethan Lanthier was charged with seven runs on five hits and two walks before being removed with two outs in the first inning. Harry Genth delivered a three-run double during the Mussels' early outburst.

 Mets Answer With Five-Run First Inning

 St. Lucie immediately responded with five runs against Fort Myers starter Matt Barr in the bottom of the first. Antonio Jimenez, Branny De Oleo and Simon Juan each recorded RBI hits to cut the deficit to 8-5.

 The Mighty Mussels added three runs against Franyel Diaz in the third inning. Ramiro Dominguez drove in two with a single, and Byron Chourio hit a solo home run to extend the Fort Myers lead to 11-5.

 Trey Snyder helped St. Lucie pull closer in the fourth inning with an unconventional trip around the bases. Snyder's ground-ball single was mishandled by shortstop Quetin Young, who then committed a throwing error that allowed Snyder to score and another run to cross the plate.

 The play cut the Mussels' lead to 11-7.

 Guzman Homers Twice

 Randy Guzman hit a two-run homer against Ramiro Villanueva in the fifth inning to bring the Mets within two runs.

 Villanueva later hit consecutive batters and was ejected. St. Lucie loaded the bases with one out, but reliever Adam Falinski retired Elian Pena on a popout and Snyder on a groundout to preserve the 11-9 Fort Myers advantage.

 Young answered with a three-run home run over the batter's eye in the sixth, pushing the Mussels' lead to 14-9.

 Guzman responded again in the bottom half of the inning, launching a three-run homer to make it 14-12.

 He finished the game 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, six RBIs and two runs scored.

 Ninth-Inning Rally Falls One Run Short

 Ricardo Paez opened the ninth inning with a solo home run that gave Fort Myers a 15-13 lead and provided what proved to be a crucial insurance run.

 Francisco Toledo scored on a wild pitch and throwing error with one out in the bottom of the ninth. Marco Vargas then homered to right field with two outs, pulling St. Lucie within one run at 15-14.

 Brent Francisco struck out Chase Meggers to end the game and record his third save.

 Michael Hilker Jr. earned the win after pitching 2 1/3 scoreless innings of relief for Fort Myers. Lanthier took the loss.

 Jimenez went 2-for-3 with two walks and three runs scored. Vargas, De Oleo and Juan added two hits apiece.

 The Mets fell to 10-18 in the second half and 43-51 overall. The Mighty Mussels improved to 14-14 in the second half and 51-42 overall.

 The teams will conclude their series Sunday at Clover Park. First pitch is scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

cards.headline: Zayas Homers Twice as St. Lucie Mets Cruise Past Mighty Mussels
cards.teaser:
Julio Zayas homered twice and Trey Snyder continued his hot stretch at the plate as the St. Lucie Mets defeated the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels 8-2 Tuesday night at Clover Park.

The
cards.body:
Julio Zayas homered twice and Trey Snyder continued his hot stretch at the plate as the St. Lucie Mets defeated the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels 8-2 Tuesday night at Clover Park.

The victory in the series opener was St. Lucie's fifth win in its last six games.

Zayas finished 3-for-4 with his fifth and sixth home runs of the season.

Snyder also went 3-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and a run scored. He has collected seven hits over his last two games.

St. Lucie starter Conner Ware pitched three scoreless innings, allowing no runs while striking out four.

Emilio Obispo earned the win after allowing two runs on two hits over four innings. He walked three and struck out three.

Zack Mack pitched a scoreless eighth inning before Elwis Mijares worked the ninth and induced a 4-6-3 double play to end the game.

The Mets improved to 9-14 in the second half and 42-47 overall. The Mighty Mussels fell to 10-13 in the second half and 47-41 overall.

cards.headline: Messi bathed Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot, now they meet in World Cup final
cards.teaser: A 2007 charity calendar photo shoot paired teenage Lionel Messi with infant Lamine Yamal. Now 19 years later, they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, took the photos after Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate.

 Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

 Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation.

 The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Museum of Art hosts free friendship bracelet workshop with recycled fishing line
hero.body:
The Vero Beach Museum of Art will host a free Second Saturday program on Aug. 8 featuring hands-on activities that transform discarded fishing line into friendship bracelets. The program runs from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. and includes docent-led gallery tours, studio art projects and lessons about protecting local marine life.

Coastal Connections will lead the fishing line bracelet activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium. Participants can learn about the organization's Fishing Line Recycling Program while creating bracelets from line collected from local waterways. The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp.

The Nature in Layers art activity for children connects to the museum's current exhibitions through the Museum Studios family program. Visitors can tour James Prosek: At Work in the Holmes Gallery and Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases in the Schumann and Titelman galleries throughout the day.

Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections, said the partnership demonstrates how the organization works with the community to introduce marine conservation and environmental protection. The museum offers free admission throughout the day on Second Saturdays. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing sea turtle survival by educating and connecting people to the environment.

cards.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
cards.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
cards.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. Led by Summer Faerman, the program connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts.

 The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

 Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

 As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 hot meals daily to children at 35 summer sites
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach is serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program while school is out.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Food Bank is serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program, according to Food Bank leaders. The nonprofit organization supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County while school is out for the summer. During a live Shining A Light broadcast on WPTV, CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen, where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county.

 The organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone. According to the Palm Beach County Food Bank, hunger doesn't take a summer break, highlighting the need for continued support during the summer months. The Summer BreakSpot program provides free meals to children and teens 18 and younger during the summer when school cafeterias are closed. Food Bank leaders said the meals are distributed through partner locations across Palm Beach County to help families facing food insecurity during the summer. Kendall said the Food Bank's partnership with Summer BreakSpot helps ensure children continue receiving nutritious meals while school is out.

 During the broadcast, viewers got a close look at the large-scale kitchen operation responsible for preparing meals daily. Chef Barg walked viewers through the food production process, showing how culinary teams prepare, package and organize meals before they are loaded onto delivery trucks. The loading dock operation featured drivers and volunteers preparing for morning deliveries to Summer BreakSpot sites throughout Palm Beach County. The Palm Beach County Food Bank said volunteers and community support are critical to maintaining the program during the busy summer season.

 The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach. Food Bank leaders said the organization continues seeking volunteers, donations and community partnerships to support its mission of reducing childhood hunger in Palm Beach County. Families looking for Summer BreakSpot meal locations can find participating sites throughout the county during the summer months.

hero.headline: Florida carries out first double execution in more than six decades, including second-oldest prisoner in U.S. history
hero.body:
Florida executed two men on Tuesday, becoming the first state in nearly a decade to carry out two executions in a single day. The second execution was of 80-year-old Dominick Anthony Occhicone, the second-oldest inmate known to receive a lethal injection in modern U.S. history. Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis, who has the authority under Florida law to set execution dates, scheduled both executions hours apart earlier this month.

Occhicone was pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m. at Florida State Prison near Starke following a three-drug injection. His execution came nearly five hours after James Aren Duckett, 68, a former police officer convicted of raping and drowning 11-year-old Teresa McAbee in central Florida in 1987, received a lethal dose in the same death chamber. Duckett was pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m. and declined to make a final statement. Occhicone, convicted of fatally shooting his ex-girlfriend's parents in June 1986, apologized to the victims' families and his own family in his final words. He is the oldest prisoner executed in Florida since the state began modern record-keeping a century ago. Nationwide, only 83-year-old Walter Moody Jr., executed in Alabama in 2018, was older.

The executions mark the 11th and 12th carried out by Florida this year. The state has conducted more executions in 2026 than all other states combined. DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the U.S. reinstatement of the death penalty in 1976. Another execution is scheduled for August. Nationwide, 19 executions have been carried out this year, with Florida accounting for 12. The last time a state carried out two executions in one day was in 2017, when Arkansas put two men to death three hours apart.

Florida Department of Corrections records show multiple executions on a single day were more common in the past, with the last occurring in 1964. The U.S. Supreme Court denied last appeals from both men Tuesday. DeSantis has rarely commented on the pace of executions, previously noting some on death row had committed crimes as far back as the 1980s. He said last year that justice delayed is justice denied. All Florida executions are by injection of a sedative, a paralytic and a drug that stops the heart.

cards.headline: Fishback stays on Florida Republican primary ballot after judge rejects Collins residency challenge
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback demanded that Lt. Gov. Jay Collins resign after a judge ruled Collins failed to present enough evidence to remove Fishback from the August primary ballot.
cards.body:
Circuit Judge David Frank ruled Monday that Collins failed to present enough evidence to overcome Florida's legal presumptions favoring continued residency and access to the ballot. Collins had argued that Fishback failed to satisfy the Florida Constitution's requirement that a governor reside in the state for the seven years preceding the general election. Collins pointed to records showing Fishback voted in Washington during the 2020 presidential election, filed D.C. resident income-tax returns and signed mortgage documents identifying a condominium there as his principal residence.

Fishback testified that he never intended to abandon Florida as his permanent home and described the Washington property as a second residence or investment. Frank acknowledged that Fishback's filings could potentially create legal or regulatory consequences in Washington but found they did not establish that Fishback intended to surrender his Florida domicile. The judge cited Fishback's Florida upbringing, family connections, drivers license, vehicle registration, voting history and business ties to the state.

Fishback turned his courtroom victory into a counterattack Tuesday, accusing Collins of abusing his office and the public trust. Collins rejected the resignation demand and mocked Fishback as a trans-Floridian. Political scientist Susan MacManus said the continued presence of Fishback, Collins and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner in the race could benefit U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, the Trump-endorsed Republican frontrunner. Recent polling has consistently shown Donalds leading, with a Cygnal survey conducted July 12 and 13 placing Donalds at 43%, Fishback at 12%, Collins at 11% and Renner at 2%. Florida's closed Republican primary is Aug. 18.

cards.headline: Over 150 Florida residents remain displaced after Bradenton assisted living roof collapse
cards.teaser: More than 150 residents remain scattered across assisted living facilities throughout the Tampa Bay area days after a partial roof collapse forced an emergency evacuation at Aviata at Bradenton Villas early Sunday morning.
cards.body:
Family members say loved ones have been placed in facilities as far south as Englewood and as far north as New Port Richey, with medical records, wheelchairs and personal belongings still trapped inside the damaged building. George Mendez, who holds power of attorney for 93-year-old Alfred Perani, said repeated phone calls to Aviata Health Group went unanswered. Perani was evacuated to a facility in Palm Harbor, and Mendez found an available bed at another facility in Bradenton but says he cannot complete the transfer without Perani's medical records.

The City of Bradenton and Manatee County provided details Monday about why the Fire Marshal ordered the emergency evacuation. The partial roof collapse compromised multiple building systems essential to safe operation, including fire protection, electrical and air conditioning systems. Damage to critical support areas necessary for resident care, combined with the inability to safely complete a full structural assessment during the emergency, made it unsafe for residents to remain. All 157 residents were evacuated by approximately 4 a.m. Sunday.

The property owner's structural engineer is responsible for evaluating the building, and any determination regarding the cause of the collapse will be based on that evaluation. The Agency for Health Care Administration is conducting site visits at the facilities where residents were relocated. All inquiries regarding individual residents, including their current locations, must be directed to Aviata due to HIPAA and other privacy requirements. Families seeking information may contact Aviata through its general information number at 800-781-9593.

cards.headline: Florida executes former police officer convicted of killing 11-year-old girl in 1987
cards.teaser: James Aren Duckett, 68, was pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m. Tuesday at Florida State Prison, the first of two executions carried out by the state in a single day.
cards.body:
Duckett was convicted of raping and drowning 11-year-old Teresa McAbee while he was working as a police officer in central Florida in 1987. He declined to make a final statement and showed no response several minutes into the execution when the prison warden shook him and shouted his name. Duckett became the 11th Florida inmate executed this year.

The girl's relatives spoke of decades of suffering after the execution. Dorthy Tula, the victim's mother, said she waited nearly 40 years to have him dead before breaking down. Tracy Mcfall-Buskirk, the girl's cousin, said the man took advantage of his badge. The execution was part of the first double execution in Florida in more than six decades and the first time any state has carried out two executions in one day since Arkansas in 2017.

Florida has now conducted 12 executions to date in 2026, more than all other states combined. Gov. Ron DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the reinstatement of the death penalty in the U.S. in 1976.

cards.headline: Florida leads nation with 12 executions in 2026 as DeSantis oversees record pace in final term
cards.teaser: Florida has now conducted 12 executions in 2026, more than all other states combined, as Gov. Ron DeSantis oversees a record pace of capital punishment at the end of his final term.
cards.body:
DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the U.S. reinstatement of the death penalty in 1976. Nationwide, the use of the death penalty had been declining for two decades, but that number has ticked up behind the increased pace in Florida. Since 2025 began, Florida has carried out nearly half the state executions across the country. Nationwide, a total of 19 executions have been carried out this year.

 DeSantis has rarely commented on the pace of executions, previously noting some on death row had committed crimes as far back as the 1980s. The governor said last year that justice delayed is justice denied and that he felt he owed it to families to make sure executions ran very smoothly. Another execution in Florida is set for August.  Floridians for Alternatives to the Death Penalty recently urged DeSantis to halt both executions carried out Tuesday, calling two in one day an unprecedented escalation of Florida's use of the death penalty. Grace Hanna, the group's executive director, said Florida continues to expand the use of capital punishment, despite mounting evidence that it is not what Floridians want. DeSantis has not said why he scheduled two executions hours apart.

hero.headline: Martin County commissioners move to rewrite shark fishing rules after complaints about drones and chum
hero.teaser: Martin County commissioners are rewriting rules on fishing from public beaches after complaints that shark fishermen are using drones and remote-controlled boats to drop chum offshore and lure sharks closer to swimming areas.
hero.body:
County attorneys told commissioners Tuesday that Florida law allows fishing from public beaches and takes precedence over conflicting county ordinances. Commissioners now plan to repeal or rewrite portions of the county's existing law and replace them with restrictions based on public safety. The county banned fishing from public beaches years ago, but local fishermen have recently pushed back, arguing the rule amounts to government overreach.

Residents who addressed commissioners said they are concerned fishermen are putting swimmers at risk by attracting sharks close to shore. Chumming directly from the beach is already prohibited under Florida law, but commissioners heard complaints that some fishermen are using drones or remote-controlled boats to carry bait offshore before dropping it into the water, potentially allowing them to skirt the state restriction.

County attorneys recommended drafting a new ordinance that complies with state fishing laws while relying on the county's authority to protect public safety and welfare. Under the proposal, fishing could be prohibited from county beaches during lifeguard hours, when swimmers are most likely to be in the water. The revised ordinance would also prohibit fishing from boat docks while boats are being launched or returning to shore. Commissioners directed county staff to draft the new ordinance and bring it back for a future vote.

cards.headline: Homestead exemption expansion could force higher insurance premiums for Martin County residents near closed fire stations
cards.teaser: Martin County Commissioner James Blake Capps warned that if three fire stations close due to budget cuts from the proposed homestead exemption expansion, many residents would end up paying higher homeowner's insurance premiums.
cards.body:
Capps said residents within five miles of a fire station receive a break on homeowner's insurance, but those farther than five miles away pay higher premiums. If the county shuts down three fire stations, a lot of people would end up paying more for homeowner's insurance. Martin County Fire Rescue projects it could lose 116 firefighters over the next two years, about one-third of its workforce, because of reduced property tax revenue tied to the proposed amendment.

Fire Rescue leaders discussed potential operational changes if those revenue reductions occur. Previous county projections have outlined possible station closures, reductions to specialized teams including HAZMAT, Technical Rescue, the dive team and LifeStar, and delays in replacing equipment. County leaders have previously said the department has few options to absorb the projected revenue loss because about 93% of the Fire Rescue budget is dedicated to personnel.

Capps also said there would have to be a no-overtime policy for all fire rescue personnel, which means no backfilling of stations with personnel and would result in randomized brownouts of stations. Voters will have the final say on the constitutional amendment during the November general election. No vote on firefighter layoffs or fire station closures is expected during Tuesday's meeting.

cards.headline: Martin County fire chief cites Texas Camp Mystic flooding as example of dangers from delayed emergency response
cards.teaser: Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli pointed to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in Texas as an example of the delays that can occur when a community must rely on outside resources for specialized emergency response.
cards.body:
Cianciulli said Texas officials had to call for outside assets, resulting in a 14-hour response to start mitigating that scene. He told commissioners that Martin County is currently in a position where if any incident occurs, the department is able to do an immediate mitigation without wasting any second. The chief warned that the funding loss from the proposed homestead exemption expansion could force Martin County to eliminate specialized teams responsible for hazardous materials incidents, technical rescues and dive operations.

The department could then have to request assistance from neighboring agencies in Palm Beach or St. Lucie counties, potentially increasing response times. During public comment, one resident and a commissioner questioned whether reducing employee salaries could help address the potential shortfall. Cianciulli responded, saying Martin County already has difficulty recruiting trained firefighter-paramedics because departments farther south offer better compensation.

Cianciulli advised residents to learn as much as possible about the proposal and its potential effects before casting their ballots in November. The measure, which will go before Florida voters in November, could lower property tax bills for homeowners but local governments have warned that it could also reduce revenue used to pay for public services.

cards.headline: Big Taste of Martin County fundraiser to support Big Brothers Big Sisters mentoring programs Oct. 6
cards.teaser: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties will hold its Big Taste of Martin County fundraiser on Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart.
cards.body:
Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties is preparing for the return of Big Taste of Martin County, a food and spirits event scheduled for Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart. The annual fundraiser brings together local restaurants, chefs and community partners to support mentoring programs for children across the Treasure Coast.

 Guests can sample food, wine and beer from area businesses while participating restaurants compete for Big Taste awards and local bragging rights. The event helps fund mentorship opportunities for children who are currently waiting to be matched with a mentor, known as a Big. Spritz Stuart plans to feature several menu items during the event, including a Tuscan salmon dish, a smash burger and a specialty cocktail called the Fig & Flame.

 Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties serves children and families throughout Palm Beach and Martin counties through one-on-one mentoring relationships designed to support academic achievement, confidence and personal growth. Community members can support the mission by purchasing tickets, attending the event or volunteering to become a mentor.

cards.teaser: Martin County Commissioner James Blake Capps said a no-overtime policy for fire rescue personnel could result in randomized brownouts of stations if the tax amendment passes.
