cards.headline: Martin County projects $16.5 million annual Fire Rescue budget loss under proposed homestead exemption
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Rescue projects its annual budget would decline by $9.5 million in the first year if voters approve expanded homestead exemptions in November.
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue projects its annual budget would decline by $9.5 million in the first year under a proposed expansion of Florida's homestead exemption. By the second year, the annual loss would reach $16.5 million, a 22% reduction from the department's current budget. Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli presented the planning exercise during Tuesday's commission meeting.

 Under the scenario, Fire Rescue could close Station 18 on Britt Road, Station 33 in Hobe Sound, and Station 23 on Kanner Highway. The department could be forced to lay off as many as 116 firefighters by the second year, equivalent to one of the department's three shifts. The funding loss could force Martin County to eliminate specialized teams responsible for hazardous materials incidents, technical rescues and dive operations.

 Cianciulli pointed to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in Texas as an example of delays that can occur when a community must rely on outside resources. In an interview after the meeting, Cianciulli said they had to call for outside assets, a 14 hour response to start mitigating that scene. He said Martin County is in a position where if any incident happens, they are able to do an immediate mitigation without wasting any second.

hero.headline: New $70 million K-8 school breaks ground in Fort Pierce, will consolidate three St. Lucie County campuses
hero.body:
A groundbreaking ceremony Tuesday marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one state-of-the-art facility. The new school will be built on land behind Dan McCarty Middle School and is expected to welcome between 1,500 and 1,800 students when it opens. It will consolidate Dan McCarty Middle, St. Lucie Elementary and Lawnwood Elementary into a single campus.

Superintendent Jon Prince said the project is moving forward on time, on budget, and on schedule. The new facility will feature state-of-the-art technology and serve the north part of St. Lucie County. The decision to consolidate comes as the existing schools show their age. All three were built in the 1950s and 1960s. Dan McCarty Middle Principal Latricia Stubbs-James said some of the things in the buildings are antiquated and that students in the northern part of the county are getting the attention they deserve and need.

The district is funding the $70 million project in part by selling the properties where the three older schools currently stand, offsetting the cost of maintaining aging buildings. Prince said the K-8 model is already proven across the district, which operates 11 other K-8 schools. Attendance is better, test scores are better and grades are better in the K-8s, Prince said. Stubbs-James said the K-8 model offers unique benefits, allowing kindergarten students to see what it looks like to be an eighth grader or a fifth grader.

The new Fort Pierce K-8 school is expected to be completed in August 2028. Prince said the facility will be very popular in the community.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents oppose proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe, fear displacement of St. Lucie County Regional History Museum
cards.teaser: Residents and history advocates in Fort Pierce are raising concerns over a proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe, fearing the development could displace the St. Lucie County Regional History Museum.
cards.body:
The Port of Fort Pierce master plan draft for 2026 calls for replacing the existing area at Museum Pointe with large floating docks designed for mega yachts, along with a clubhouse, an event center and a water taxi connecting to Harbour Pointe to the north. The plan also proposes relocating the history museum.

Terry Howard, a passionate advocate for St. Lucie County's history, expressed disbelief over the proposed changes. This is a gem for the area, and I just can't believe they want to put mega yachts here, he said. The museum, it's our culture. It's the center for our culture for this county. Howard has started a petition opposing the proposed marina, hoping to raise awareness and preserve the location and its natural surroundings.

St. Lucie County said that no plans have been approved and feedback from the board will dictate future changes, modifications and clarifications to the draft document. The draft of the master plan is expected to go before the county commission in August.

cards.headline: Three caregivers arrested after 3-month-old dies from severe dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce home
cards.teaser: A 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition after living in a Fort Pierce home with boarded windows, exposed electrical wiring and cockroaches, according to court documents and St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office investigators.
cards.body:
The investigation began in August 2025 when detectives were called to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital after the infant was brought in deceased by Robert Maxwell and Vikki Koon. The medical examiner determined the child died from dehydration and malnutrition. Detective Jennifer Diaz said in her 20 years of law enforcement, this is one of the worst cases she has ever worked. The infant's mother, Nicole Maxwell, grandfather Robert Maxwell and the grandfather's girlfriend Vikki Koon now face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse.

The child lived primarily with Maxwell and Koon while the child's mother lived at her boyfriend's home in Vero Beach. According to court documents, Koon primarily fed the infant only twice a day and admitted to investigators that when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with bay cereal mixed in. Koon told deputies she believed a newborn should have two ounces per feeding twice a day. An autopsy revealed the infant was emaciated and had a sunken abdomen and widespread lesions consistent with severe dehydration and malnutrition.

Court documents describe the mobile home as having windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring and live and dead cockroaches throughout. A neighbor named Suzan said the conditions looked unlivable and she would often see one of the other children walking around the neighborhood asking for water. Nicole Maxwell's other children who were living inside the mobile home are now in foster care. All three suspects remain in custody.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police seek public's help identifying suspects in Recreation Center vandalism, vehicle burglaries
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police are asking for the public's help identifying people shown in surveillance images connected to two separate investigations involving vandalism and vehicle burglaries.
cards.body:
Police said the vandalism occurred at about 4 p.m. July 24 at the Fort Pierce Recreation Center, located at 903 S. According to the department, an unidentified woman was captured on camera damaging city property. Multiple air-conditioning units, a trailer and a storage shed were damaged.

The second investigation involves a series of vehicle burglaries reported during the overnight hours of July 27 in the Lawnwood Circle area. Police said the burglaries occurred in the 1300 block of Nebraska Avenue and the 1300 block of Peppertree Trail, primarily between 2 a.m. and 5 a.m. Several vehicles were burglarized. Some had been left unlocked, while others had windows smashed to gain entry. Surveillance footage showed several people in the area wearing hoodies, shorts and backpacks.

The department stressed that the vandalism and vehicle burglary cases are separate investigations. Anyone who recognizes the people pictured or has information about either case is asked to contact Fort Pierce police at 772-467-6800 or 772-462-6800. Anonymous tips can be submitted to Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at tcwatch.org. Police also reminded residents to lock their vehicles, remove valuables from plain view and report suspicious activity immediately.

cards.headline: Man forced to withdraw cash during armed robbery at Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: A man using a Wells Fargo ATM became the victim of an armed robbery after two men forced him to pull out cash before fleeing the scene on foot.
cards.body:
The Fort Pierce Police Department said the robbery happened Sunday at about 8:38 p.m. Two men approached the victim, and one of them displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash.

Officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department responded to the scene, established a perimeter, and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects. The suspects were not located. Police described them as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie could lose $48 million over two years if property tax amendment passes
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie officials say the city would lose over $48 million in property taxes over the next two years if a constitutional amendment on the November ballot passes.
cards.body:
During a summer budget workshop Thursday at the Port St. Lucie Community Center, City Manager Jesus Merejo told the City Council the city would lose the revenue if the item passes in November. To prepare for the potential hit, the city is deferring projects and holding the line on hiring. Port St. Lucie says it won't fund 184 requested positions, worth $28.3 million, including 25 new police officers and parks staff the city had already planned to add this year to keep up with growth at Torino Regional Park and the new BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park.

City employees also won't get a cost-of-living raise in the coming budget. On the capital side, the $7.8 million in canceled projects includes a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to I-95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park, and parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park, along with construction on a new City Hall and parking garage. Brad Keen, the director of the parks and recreation department, warned of deferred maintenance when you don't have the people in the parks to maintain them at the level the city has been accustomed to.

The proposal, known as Amendment 3, is headed to Florida voters on the November 3, 2026 ballot. If approved, it would raise the state's homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 starting in January 2027, and to $250,000 in January 2028. Because it's a constitutional amendment, it needs at least 60% approval from voters to pass. Scott Samples with the city said the council will reconvene shortly after the November 3rd election to determine next steps, whether the proposal is passed or fails.

cards.headline: Two men flee Port St. Lucie police at 80 mph, one found hiding on roof of occupied home
cards.teaser: A suspected drunk driver fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran, with one suspect later found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving. Instead of pulling over, the driver accelerated to nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone on Southwest Becker Road. Police said the driver and passenger weaved in and out of traffic, ignored traffic signs and signals, then abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot.

A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home. The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46.

Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

hero.headline: Indian River County Fire Rescue visits Dodgertown Elementary for career fair
hero.teaser: Firefighters from Indian River County Fire Rescue spent time with students at Dodgertown Elementary on Tuesday, sharing what it is like to serve the community.
hero.body:
Indian River County Fire Rescue participated in a career fair at Dodgertown Elementary at 4350 43rd Street in Vero Beach on Tuesday, July 28. Firefighters spent time with students at the school, discussing what it is like to serve the community and introducing them to the various career opportunities available in the fire service.

The event gave students a chance to ask questions and see the equipment firefighters use in their daily work. Indian River County Fire Rescue posted about the visit on Facebook, describing it as a day filled with learning and inspiration. "From answering great questions to showing off our equipment, it was a fantastic day of learning and inspiration," the department said in the statement.

Fire Rescue officials said they hope the career fair will help inspire the next generation of firefighters, paramedics and public servants. The department emphasized the rewarding nature of careers in fire service during their time with the students. The firefighters shared information about serving the community and the different roles available within the department.

The career fair represented an opportunity for young students to learn about public service careers firsthand from the firefighters who perform those jobs every day. By bringing equipment to the school and taking time to answer student questions, Fire Rescue aimed to give children a better understanding of what firefighters and paramedics do to help their community.

cards.headline: Recycled fishing line to be transformed into friendship bracelets at Vero Beach Museum of Art
cards.teaser: Discarded fishing line collected from local waterways will be transformed into friendship bracelets during a free Second Saturday program at the Vero Beach Museum of Art on Aug. 8.
cards.body:
Discarded fishing line collected from local waterways will be transformed into friendship bracelets during a free Second Saturday program at the Vero Beach Museum of Art on Aug. 8. The museum is partnering with Coastal Connections for hands-on activities beginning at 10 a.m., including docent-led gallery tours and lessons about protecting local marine life.

 Coastal Connections will lead the bracelet-making activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium using recycled fishing line collected through the organization's Fishing Line Recycling Program. Participants can also learn about the program and marine conservation efforts. The Vero Beach Museum of Art has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp.

 From 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., families can take short, docent-led gallery tours through the Museum Studios family program. Visitors can participate in Nature in Layers, an art activity for children connected to the museum's exhibitions. Guests can also tour the museum's summer exhibitions, including James Prosek: At Work in the Holmes Gallery and Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases in the Schumann and Titelman galleries.

 Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing the survival of sea turtles by educating and connecting people to the environment. Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections, said the partnership with the museum is an example of working with the community to introduce marine conservation and environmental protection in unique ways.

cards.headline: 3 arrested in Fort Pierce after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition
cards.teaser: A 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in August 2025 after living in a Fort Pierce mobile home with boarded windows, exposed electrical wiring and cockroaches
cards.body:
A 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in August 2025 after living in a Fort Pierce mobile home with boarded windows, exposed electrical wiring and cockroaches, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Nicole Maxwell, 27, the infant's mother, Robert Maxwell, 61, the child's grandfather, and Vikki Koon, 38, Robert Maxwell's girlfriend, were arrested and charged with aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse nearly a year after the death.

 The investigation began in August 2025 when Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the deceased infant to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. The medical examiner determined the child died from dehydration and malnutrition, with court documents describing the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach. Koon told deputies she fed the infant only twice a day and when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with baby cereal mixed in. The infant lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon at their mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle in Fort Pierce while Nicole Maxwell lived at her boyfriend's home in Vero Beach.

 Detective Jennifer Diaz, who worked the case, said the mobile home was extremely hot with a bug infestation, lack of food, and unsafe conditions for walking. A neighbor named Suzan said she witnessed the conditions firsthand and described the home as unlivable. Suzan said other children from the home would come to her asking for water, appearing thirsty, unbathed and wearing the same clothes every day. Nicole Maxwell's four other children, ranging in age from 2 to 10 years old, were living in the mobile home and have been placed in foster care through the Department of Children and Families.

 Detective Diaz said the investigation took nearly a year because the case required outside experts and additional testing. Koon and Robert Maxwell are being held in the St. Lucie County Jail each on $1.5 million bond. Nicole Maxwell was arrested on July 23 at a home in the 300 block of 12th Street SW in Vero Beach and is being held in the Indian River County Jail on no bond. Diaz emphasized the importance of reporting suspicious activity to protect children, saying tips are instrumental to keeping children safe.

cards.headline: Cyclist rides through Vero Beach on 2,600-mile journey from Key West to Maine
cards.teaser: A Boston cyclist rode through Vero Beach this week on a 2,600-mile bike ride from Key West to Maine to honor a friend lost to colorectal cancer.
cards.body:
Jay Weedall traveled to South Florida to begin the journey, with a goal of raising $50,000 for the Young Onset Colorectal Cancer Research Center. Weedall began his journey in Key West, pedaling 155 miles to Miami on day one. He set off on his second leg, a 163-mile ride to Vero Beach, after filling his hydration pack with ice to stay cool.

 Weedall is riding roughly 150 miles a day up the coast through nearly every state all the way to the Pan Mass Challenge. He will do the Pan Mass Challenge across Massachusetts on August 2 and continue to the Canadian border in Maine. By avoiding highways, Weedall says the route offers something unexpected, allowing him to experience little coastal towns along the inlets. Fans can follow Weedall's journey on the cycling app Strava.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Police Department honors service of Indian River County firefighter
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands with Indian River County Fire Rescue following the death of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach Police Department said it stands alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning the loss of Firefighter Geoffrey Lang, who passed away while off duty. The department said its thoughts are with his family, loved ones and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time and that it honors his service and the impact he made on the community.

 Indian River County Fire Rescue announced Lang's death Saturday night and thanked neighboring agencies that quickly shared messages of support following the announcement. The Sebastian Police Department said it stands alongside its brothers and sisters of Indian River County Fire Rescue as they mourn the heartbreaking loss and that Lang's dedication, courage and commitment to serving others will never be forgotten.

cards.headline: Sebastian Police, Vero Beach Police honor Indian River County firefighter Geoffrey Lang
cards.teaser: Multiple law enforcement agencies across Indian River County expressed condolences following the death of Firefighter/Paramedic Geoffrey Lang.
cards.body:
The Sebastian Police Department said it was standing alongside Indian River County Fire Rescue in mourning Lang's death. "Your bravery and service will always be remembered," the department wrote. The Vero Beach Police Department also shared its condolences, saying it stands alongside IRCFR during the difficult time.

 "Our thoughts are with his family, loved ones, and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time," the Vero Beach Police Department said. "We honor his service and the impact he made on our community." Indian River County Fire Rescue posted a photo on its Facebook page Saturday night acknowledging the end of watch for Lang.

 The Indian River County Sheriff's Office also expressed condolences. Anna Kirkland, Indian River Mosquito Control District Seat 2, said she was praying for Lang's family, friends, and the entire Indian River County Fire Rescue family. She thanked Lang for his service to the community.

cards.headline: Indian River County leaders remember firefighter Geoffrey Lang who worked out of Sebastian station
cards.teaser: Geoffrey Lang died on Saturday following a personal tragedy at his home in Sebastian, county spokeswoman Kathy Copeland said.
cards.body:
Lang, 35, was survived by his wife, two children and parents. Lang joined Indian River County Fire Rescue in 2015 and worked out of Station 9 at 13550 Roseland Road in Sebastian. Copeland said that Lang dedicated his career to serving the residents of Indian River County with professionalism and compassion. He was a valued member of the department, respected by his fellow firefighters, and known for his unwavering commitment to others.

 Indian River County Administrator John A. said that during this incredibly difficult time, the county's hearts go out to his family, friends and all who had the privilege of serving alongside him. Indian River County Fire Rescue Chief David Johnson said the department mourns the loss of one of its own and that Lang faithfully served the community for more than a decade.

 Indian River County Commission Chair Deryl Loar said Lang was a dedicated employee and the Board of County Commissioners and County Administration extends condolences to his family, friends and colleagues. All commissioners stand with Indian River Fire Rescue and remain committed to supporting the health and well-being of personnel including the importance of mental health support for first responders and their families.
